# CellEdgeR

Differential analysis of cell-type interaction motifs from spatial
coordinates.

## Overview

CellEdgeR builds per-sample Delaunay graphs, counts label-based motifs,
and fits edgeR models with Chung-Lu-style volume offsets. Volume
normalization is the main statistical model.

The tested result sets are:

- [`top_edges()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md):
  edge motifs, keyed as `E_<label1>_<label2>`.
- [`top_motifs2()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md):
  wedge and triangle motifs, keyed as `W_<center>_<leaf1>_<leaf2>` and
  `T_<label1>_<label2>_<label3>`.

Node counts are still computed internally to build exposures and
normalized submotif values, but nodes are not tested as differential
motifs. Wedges and triangles are not merged into `TP_*` triplets.

## Installation

``` r
install.packages(c("geometry", "Matrix"))
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
if (!requireNamespace("edgeR", quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install("edgeR")

devtools::install_github("GeNeHetX/CellEdgeR")
library(CellEdgeR)
```

## Typical Workflow

1.  Prepare a named list of samples. Each element is a data frame with
    numeric `x`, `y` coordinates and a cell label column.

``` r
samples_list <- make_demo_samples(n_cells = 10000, seed = 42)

metadata_df <- data.frame(
  condition = rep(c("ctrl", "treated"), each = length(samples_list) / 2),
  batch = sample(c("batch1", "batch2"), length(samples_list), replace = TRUE),
  row.names = names(samples_list)
)
```

2.  Build graphs and count motifs.

``` r
cellgraph <- build_cell_graphs(samples_list, n_cores = 4, verbose = TRUE)
cellgraph <- count_motifs_graphs(
  cellgraph,
  max_edge_len = 50,
  include_wedge = TRUE,
  n_cores = 4
)
```

[`count_motifs_graphs()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/count_motifs_graphs.md)
stores raw counts, volume exposures, volume offsets, normalized counts,
and relative counts. The stored offset mode is `volume`.

3.  Fit the differential model and extract the two result tables.

``` r
cellgraph <- motif_edger(
  cellgraph = cellgraph,
  sample_df = metadata_df,
  design_formula = "~ condition + batch"
)

results <- motif_results(cellgraph, coef = "conditiontreated")
edges_tbl <- results$edges
motifs2_tbl <- results$motifs2

head(edges_tbl)
head(motifs2_tbl)
```

`motifs2_tbl` includes the wedge/triangle result plus edge-submotif
columns: `edge12`, `edge13`, `edge23`, their `logFC`/`PValue`/`FDR`, and
summary columns `submotif_min_FDR` and `submotif_max_abs_logFC`.

Before fitting,
[`motif_edger()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/motif_edger.md)
applies
[`edgeR::filterByExpr()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/edgeR/man/filterByExpr.html)
to the stacked edge/wedge/triangle count matrix. One-off motifs or
motifs with too little support are not tested and therefore do not
receive p-values or FDR values. Filter details are stored in
`cellgraph$edger$filter`.

4.  Inspect normalized counts or spatial motif plots.

``` r
norm_df <- get_motif_values(cellgraph, value = "norm")
head(norm_df)

plot_sample_graph(
  cellgraph,
  sample_name = "s1",
  max_edge_len = 50,
  motif_key = "T_a_b_c",
  motif_node_size = 0.8,
  dim_node_nonmotif = 0.1,
  alpha_node_nonmotif = 0.2,
  alpha_edge_nonmotif = 0.2
)
```

## Choosing A Pruning Threshold

The `max_edge_len` threshold controls which Delaunay edges are retained
before motif counting. Inspect the edge-length distribution and drop the
sparse tail while preserving biologically relevant local neighbors.

``` r
edge_lengths <- unlist(lapply(cellgraph$per_sample_graph, function(ps) ps$edge_len))
summary(edge_lengths)

ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(edge_len = edge_lengths), ggplot2::aes(edge_len)) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(fill = "#4477aa", alpha = 0.3, color = "#223355") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10("Edge length (log scale)") +
  ggplot2::ylab("Density") +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Edge length distribution (density, log-x)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

## Statistical Model

CellEdgeR uses volume offsets as a Chung-Lu-style exposure correction:

- Edges use label degree volumes and the sample total edge volume.
- Triangles use the three label volumes and unordered-label
  multiplicity.
- Wedges use center-label degree-pair exposure plus leaf-label volumes,
  with an equal-leaf correction.

The edgeR QL model tests differential motif rates after this exposure
correction. This is not a simple test of raw or normalized boxplot
medians.

## Tips

- Use `include_wedge = TRUE` when you want both wedges and triangles in
  [`top_motifs2()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md).
- Provide `boundary`/`is_boundary` columns or `erosion_cells` if
  boundary motifs should be excluded.
- Record `max_edge_len` and `offset_version` from `cellgraph$parameters`
  for reproducibility.
- Use
  `get_motif_values(cellgraph, value = "norm", include_submotifs = TRUE)`
  to plot a motif with its edge submotifs.
- Use
  [`motif_space_size()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/motif_space_size.md)
  to summarize the possible tested edge/wedge/triangle label space.

## Main Functions

- [`build_cell_graphs()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/build_cell_graphs.md):
  Build per-sample Delaunay graphs from coordinates and labels.
- [`count_motifs_graphs()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/count_motifs_graphs.md):
  Count node, edge, triangle, and optional wedge motifs and compute
  volume offsets.
- [`merge_motif_objs()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/merge_motif_objs.md):
  Merge motif objects and recompute volume offsets.
- [`motif_edger()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/motif_edger.md):
  Fit the volume-offset edgeR model.
- [`top_edges()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md):
  Return ranked edge motifs.
- [`top_motifs2()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md):
  Return ranked wedge and triangle motifs with edge-submotif statistics.
- [`motif_results()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md):
  Return `edges` and `motifs2` in one named list.
- [`get_motif_values()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/get_motif_values.md):
  Return raw or volume-normalized motif values.
- [`plot_sample_graph()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/plot_sample_graph.md):
  Plot one sample graph and highlight a motif.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`build_cell_graphs()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/build_cell_graphs.md)
  : Build cached cell graphs for motif counting
- [`count_motifs_graphs()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/count_motifs_graphs.md)
  : Count cell-type motifs on Delaunay graphs
- [`get_motif_values()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/get_motif_values.md)
  : Retrieve motif values (raw, normalized)
- [`get_norm_counts()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/get_norm_counts.md)
  : Retrieve normalized counts as a single data frame
- [`make_demo_samples()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/make_demo_samples.md)
  : Create a synthetic dataset for quick testing
- [`merge_motif_objs()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/merge_motif_objs.md)
  : Merge motif objects
- [`motif_edger()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/motif_edger.md)
  : Differential motif testing with edgeR
- [`motif_space_size()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/motif_space_size.md)
  : Count the number of possible tested motif labels
- [`plot_motif_artifact_check()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/plot_motif_artifact_check.md)
  : Artifact check: residuals versus edge density
- [`plot_motif_slope_test()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/plot_motif_slope_test.md)
  : Slope test for geometric scaling
- [`plot_motif_volcano()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/plot_motif_volcano.md)
  : Volcano plot for motif differential results
- [`plot_motif_volcano_triptych()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/plot_motif_volcano_triptych.md)
  : Triptych volcano with ordered motif side panels
- [`plot_sample_graph()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/plot_sample_graph.md)
  : Plot a sample graph with highlighted motifs
- [`top_edges()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md)
  [`top_motifs2()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md)
  [`top_triplets()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md)
  [`motif_results()`](https://GeNeHetX.github.io/CellEdgeR/reference/top_edges.md)
  : Top motif results
